findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp?source=mcp-registry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: web_read_batch, vendor_intelligence, email_auth_check, search_utilities, get_utility_details, network_capabilities · Private data: entity_normalize, vendor_intelligence · Public sink: vendor_intelligence, email_auth_check, network_capabilities.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: web_read_batch, vendor_intelligence, email_auth_check, search_utilities, get_utility_details, network_capabilities · Private data: entity_normalize, vendor_intelligence · Public sink: vendor_intelligence, email_auth_check, network_capabilities

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "json_repair" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
